areas.label: Recover target traversal and completion effects
areas.evidence: The former register-u16 r7 counter makes agbcc emit a player-target list read from address 0x34. With an ordinary counter, 276 bounded original-ROM comparisons pass: stubbed call arguments, request snapshots, EWRAM/IWRAM effects, callee-saved registers and SP. Cases include local/remote player owners, modes 0/1/6/7, no/player/enemy target lists, delayed timers, readiness/completion waits, cancellation, energy boundaries and early enemy-owner aborts. Restoring only the counter pin reproduces the invalid read in case (owner 0, local 0, mode 1, player targets). The full enemy-owner continuation and all game states remain unproven. Private reproducer: build/try/goal-6C568-emulate.py; negative control: build/try/goal-6C568-regression-control.py.

areas.label: Audit widths, aliases and call lifetimes
areas.evidence: The player wait path reads world flags at state+4 as u16, matching the original LDRH. Its complement mask is computed before the loop, and both arguments to sub_0806898C use one saved request-pointer view. No new hard-register binding or empty ASM constraint was added; the unsafe final-counter binding was removed. Existing narrow bindings and the enemy-owner/player-pointer contract still need a complete audit.

areas.label: Recover stack homes and register allocation
areas.evidence: Real-module heuristic distance improves from 683 to 677, but size changes from 2196 to 2208 bytes versus original 2184; frame stays 176 versus original 168. A distance-672 variant retains the demonstrated bad counter pin and is rejected. Grouping stack scalars into the descriptor frame, splitting its arrays, forcing origin/mode registers, widening mode and making the owner volatile were rejected after whole-function comparisons. SP+0xA8 caches the xs base; SP+0xAC holds the player count, not a second pointer. Preserve the valid counter repair rather than choosing a smaller unsafe draft.
